groundTruthNotes.analysis: The exposed method has signature 'load()V' — zero parameters, void return. In Capacitor, load() is the standard Plugin lifecycle hook called once at plugin initialization (see capacitorjs.com/docs/plugins/android — 'The load() method is the proper place to initialize the class instance with the Capacitor bridge object'). It does NOT accept any URL, path, or other JavaScript-controlled input. The native-bridge.js only ever calls CapacitorHttpAndroidInterface.isEnabled() (a boolean check); actual HTTP requests flow through cap.nativePromise('CapacitorHttp', 'request', ...) via the standard plugin message channel, NOT through this @JavascriptInterface surface. The JS SNIPPETS field is empty, confirming no in-app JS reaches this bridge directly with attacker-controllable data. Therefore, any finding that posits load() loading attacker-controlled URLs, reading files via path traversal, executing JavaScript from a URL, or leaking PII as a function of arguments to load() is fabricated — the method takes no arguments. 'No vulnerability' is the correct verdict for this callsite given the context provided.
